business_summary.text: Netweb Technologies India Limited is an Indian OEM offering high-end computing solutions (HCS), supercomputing systems, private cloud, and AI systems.

call_points.text: Management highlighted strong structural tailwinds in AI systems and supercomputing infrastructure demand.
Execution window extended to 16-20 weeks from 8-12 weeks earlier.
Existing facilities can support ₹3,000-plus crore turnover; no major new capex guided.
Net debt ₹199.9 Cr at June 30; first positive debt closing in many quarters.
12-month enabling resolution for growth capital, for working capital only, no M&A; nothing raised yet.
Memory prices not seen softening for a couple of quarters to a year; inventory acts as a hedge.
₹430 Cr of the ₹1,600 Cr strategic order was executed in Q1FY27.
R&D team of 125 people; R&D fully expensed, not capitalised.
Management declined to give a segment-wise pipeline breakup or quantify R&D spend on physical AI and quantum.
The company entered FY27 with a firm order book of around ₹2,100 crores and an L1 inclusive order book of ₹2,400 crores.

guidance.statement: We are guiding a revenue growth of 35% to 40% over the next couple of years.
Operating EBITDA margin to remain between 13% and 14%
60% of the ₹10,410 Cr pipeline expected to convert over 18-24 months

operating_notes.text: Launched Tyrone ParallelStor Velox unified data platform to target AI data pipeline bottlenecks.
Launched Tyrone ParallelStor Velox unified data platform for AI and HPC infrastructure.
Installed 7,000+ accelerator/GPU-based AI systems and 600+ HPC systems.
AI systems contributed 43.4% of total operating revenue in financial year '26.
CRISIL upgraded long-term bank facilities rating to Crisil A+/Stable and enhanced total rated facilities to ₹700 crore.
Order book of ₹2,506.94 Cr plus L1 of ₹848.05 Cr at 30 June 2026, with a pipeline of ₹10,410 Cr.
Execution window extended to 16-20 weeks from 8-12 weeks earlier.
Inventory days rose to 110 in June from 86 in March on raw-material stocking; receivable days improved to 78 from 86.
